prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The five depth frames show a narrow shop interior extending several metres ahead, with the floor and doorway receding centrally and display surfaces along both sides; brighter regions indicate the nearest surfaces, especially the camera wearer's hand and phone at roughly 0.2–0.5 m. Darker upper and central regions generally correspond to walls, reflections, clothing, and the distant doorway at roughly 3–6 m, while nearby display fixtures appear about 0.5–2 m away. Across the sequence, the phone and hand shift from the lower-left toward the lower-right while the viewpoint turns right, and nearby fixtures slide laterally rather than showing a clear approach or retreat. Depth discontinuities make occlusion boundaries and near-versus-far structure easier to see than in RGB, but reflective mirrors, dark clothing, bright saturated regions, and the thin diagonal stripe produce implausible or ambiguous depths, so reliable distances between people cannot be recovered.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation identifies a nearby cell phone at roughly 0.2–0.5 m in most frames, several person masks, occasional potted plants, and isolated TV or laptop labels; it separates overlapping foreground shapes that are difficult to distinguish in RGB. The phone stays low in the view and moves from left toward right as the camera turns, while person-labelled regions shift from the centre-right to the far left or cluster around the phone and hand; some masks partly leave the bottom and side borders. Where the masks are plausible, they show the phone in front of the wearer and distant upright figures several metres farther away, with foreground hands or arms occluding portions of the phone and background. The map is highly unreliable: it labels reflections, clothing, hands, fixtures, and parts of the phone as separate people or incorrect object classes, fragments single objects, and provides no dependable facing direction, gaze, metric distance, or arm-reach relationship beyond the clearly near handheld phone.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is entirely black in all five frames, so it supplies no detected body or hand joints and supports no direct estimate of posture, facing direction, gaze, reach, or distances between people. It also cannot resolve whether person-like regions in the RGB and segmentation are real people, reflections, mannequins, or partial bodies, nor can it show occlusions or which limbs extend out of view. Across the sequence it shows no trackable approach, retreat, or turning, despite the RGB indicating that the camera viewpoint rotates and the foreground phone changes horizontal position. Its absence of detections is itself evidence that pose estimation failed or had insufficient visible body structure here, making this map unreliable for spatial interpretation.
